brackets.note: Single and joint from Tax Foundation, head of household from PolicyEngine. Both show the 2026 cut of 0.1 points on the bottom five rates. Not yet read from New York's own 2026 publication.

earnedIncomeCredit.note: "thirty percent for taxable years beginning in two thousand three and thereafter" of the federal credit, refundable for full-year residents. The statute reduces it by the household credit, a small credit for low incomes that is not modeled, so the two roughly cancel and the full 30% is given. It would drop to 20% if a federal funding "reversion event" were certified, and none was found.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: New York earned income credit

childCredits.section: Tax Law 606(c-1)(1-a)(B) and (C); 2025 Form IT-213 lines 6 to 8
childCredits.note: For 2026 and 2027: $1,000 per child under four plus $500 per child aged four to sixteen, refundable. The total is reduced by $16.50 for each $1,000 of federal AGI over $110,000 (joint) or $75,000 (single, head of household). The statute has no "or fraction" wording and the 2025 form rounds AGI down to the nearest $1,000 first, so only whole thousands count. The 2026 form was not out on 2026-11-12. From 2028 the credit reverts to the old formula, so this entry must change then.
childCredits.name: Empire State child credit

standardDeduction.note: Single and joint from Tax Foundation, head of household from PolicyEngine. These amounts are not indexed.

personalExemption.note: New York has a dependent exemption only. No exemption for the filer or spouse.

benefitRecapture.note: The IT-201 tax computation worksheets, as encoded by PolicyEngine. The base and increment amounts are tied to the bracket rates and thresholds, so they must be redone whenever those change. PolicyEngine's amounts may predate the 2026 rate cut on the lower brackets. Regenerate from the 2026 IT-201 instructions when published. Checked against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 with oracle/compare.py on 2026-11-12.

rules.note: Payroll flag read on the state's pages: paid family leave is 0.432% of wages up to $411.91 a year for 2026, and disability is 0.5% of wages up to $0.60 a week. Local flag read on the Department of Taxation's New York City and Yonkers page. Recapture note is from Tax Foundation footnote (i). Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions.
notes: New York City and Yonkers levy their own resident income taxes. Not modeled.
New York takes back the benefit of its lower brackets from filers with AGI over $107,650. This is included.
Employees pay 0.432% of wages for paid family leave, up to $411.91 a year, and up to $0.60 a week for disability insurance. Not included.
Not modeled: New York's household credit, up to about $100 for low incomes, and the matching reduction it makes to the earned income credit.
maintainerNotes: From the PolicyEngine comparison run on 2026-11-12 (oracle/compare.py): recapture gaps were -$140 (single $120,000), -$1,984 (single $250,000), -$282 (joint $150,000), -$1,140 (joint $300,000). The recapture depends on taxable income and AGI together, so it does not fit an AGI-only schedule.

From the PolicyEngine comparison run on 2026-11-12 (oracle/compare.py): our New York tax was $1,000 higher for a joint filer with two children at $90,000 and $500 higher for a head of household with one child at $60,000.

Replaced on 2026-11-12 when the rule was modeled: Not modeled: New York's tax benefit recapture, which takes back the benefit of the lower brackets from higher earners. Tax here is understated above roughly $107,650 of AGI, by about $140 at $120,000 and about $2,000 at $250,000 for a single filer.
